question: A patient is having a panic attack and breathing way too fast. What are they at risk for?

options.A: Metabolic acidosis
options.B: Metabolic alkalosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Respiratory acidosis

explanation: Spot on! Breathing too fast blows off too much carbon dioxide. Losing too much acid makes the blood basic (alkaline), causing respiratory alkalosis.

question: Why does bruising often show up a day or two after a sprain?

options.A: Infection has set into the joint capsule causing skin discoloration
options.B: The body is reacting negatively to the prescribed pain medication
options.C: Excessive synovial fluid is pushing pigments to the skin surface
options.D: Blood leaks from injured small blood vessels into the surrounding soft tissue

explanation: When tiny blood vessels tear during a sprain, the blood seeps out and slowly travels toward the surface of the skin, creating that classic bruise.

question: Why do we measure strict intake and output (I&O) for a critically ill patient?

options.A: To determine how much food the patient likes to eat
options.B: To monitor kidney function and fluid balance status
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bill for fluids used
options.D: To prevent the patient from feeling thirsty

explanation: Spot on! Tracking what goes in and out helps you catch early signs of fluid overload or kidney trouble before they become dangerous.

question: Which bed position is best for instantly helping an out-of-breath patient expand their lungs?

options.A: Trendelenburg position
options.B: High-Fowler's position
options.C: Prone lying position
options.D: Flat supine position

explanation: Sitting upright in High-Fowler's position uses gravity to push abdominal organs downward, giving the lungs more room to fill with air. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which gland releases prolactin into the blood to make milk?

options.A: Thyroid gland
options.B: Posterior pituitary gland
options.C: Adrenal cortex
options.D: Anterior pituitary gland

explanation: You got it! The anterior pituitary releases prolactin whenever the baby suckles, telling your body to keep making milk.

question: Which physical sign is a classic warning flag that a patient might be experiencing abuse?

options.A: A surgical scar from an appendectomy performed years ago
options.B: Unexplained bruises in various stages of healing
options.C: Age-related thinning of the skin on the forearms
options.D: Symmetrical skin rashes caused by a new soap

explanation: You got it! Bruises looking fresh, yellow, and faded all at once usually point to repeated trauma over time, not a single clumsy accident.

question: Which team member takes the lead in evaluating a resident's nutrition and managing special diets?

options.A: Registered dietitian
options.B: Social worker
options.C: Physical therapist
options.D: Activities director

explanation: Registered dietitians assess nutrition needs, track weight changes, and design healthy meal plans tailored to each resident.

question: What is a primary focus of health assessment in older adults?

options.A: Monitoring pediatric developmental milestones
options.B: Evaluating cognitive function and fall risks
options.C: Checking birth weight and Apgar scores
options.D: Screening exclusively for adolescent scoliosis

explanation: Older adults face unique age-related challenges like memory changes and balance issues that require targeted assessments. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h3)

question: When you gently tap and feel a patient's arm to find a good vein, what should a healthy peripheral vein feel like?

options.A: A hard, rigid cord that does not bounce back
options.B: A soft, bouncy vessel that refills after being pressed
options.C: A deep vessel that cannot be felt but looks dark blue
options.D: A pulsing vessel that moves strongly under the finger

explanation: Spot on! Healthy veins feel spongy, elastic, and refill promptly with blood after you press them. You'll get great at spotting these on the ward!

question: Why do we calculate children's drug doses based on their body weight?

options.A: Kids can't swallow adult pills
options.B: Hospital insurance requires it for kids
options.C: Children process and clear drugs differently based on size
options.D: It helps check expiration dates

explanation: Children's bodies and organs are still developing, so weight-based dosing is vital to avoid accidental overdose.

question: What is a major risk of running a complete no-blame culture?

options.A: It increases the cost of buying hospital medical equipment
options.B: It completely stops communication between doctors and nurses
options.C: It fails to hold people accountable for reckless and dangerous actions
options.D: It guarantees that nurses lose their licenses right away

explanation: Total immunity can protect unsafe, reckless behavior. Balance is key to keeping patients safe!

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing action when managing an outbreak using incubation data?

options.A: Prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics to every community resident
options.B: Calculating the probable exposure date for sick patients
options.C: Stocking adequate testing supplies for anticipated surges
options.D: Educating exposed contacts on why they need to monitor symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Giving out unnecessary antibiotics causes drug resistance. Nurses focus on tracking, educating, and supporting the community instead.

question: Which type of medication is given to treat intestinal worm infections?

options.A: Antihypertensives
options.B: Anthelmintics
options.C: Antivirals
options.D: Antifungals

explanation: Think 'anti' (against) and 'helmintic' (worms)! Anthelmintics are the specific drugs nurses administer to clear out parasitic worms.

question: Why is the Chain of Survival compared to a linked chain?

options.A: All the steps happen simultaneously in the exact same room
options.B: Every step must be performed by a medical doctor
options.C: The final step is always the most important part of treatment
options.D: If any single link fails, the overall chance of survival drops sharply

explanation: Each phase relies on the success of the previous one to keep blood flowing and restore life. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why do we perform a crossmatch test before giving a blood transfusion?

options.A: To check for direct reactions between donor cells and recipient serum
options.B: To measure the exact volume of red blood cells in the patient
options.C: To find out if the patient has any hidden infectious diseases
options.D: To determine the patient's baseline hemoglobin and hematocrit

explanation: Crossmatching is a crucial safety step! Lab staff mix donor cells and recipient serum together first to make sure they won't react violently inside the patient's body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is it important to encourage a laboring mother to empty her bladder often?

options.A: Urine samples must be tested every hour during home births
options.B: It stops the uterus from contracting too strongly
options.C: It prevents the development of chronic urinary tract infections
options.D: A full bladder can obstruct fetal descent and slow down labor

explanation: Think of the bladder like a roadblock in the pelvis! Emptying it clears the way so the baby's head can move down smoothly.

question: What makes an auto-disable syringe different from a conventional disposable syringe?

options.A: It can be washed and sterilized multiple times safely.
options.B: It locks or breaks automatically to prevent second use.
options.C: It holds a much larger volume of liquid than any other type.
options.D: It is made entirely of soft, flexible rubber material.

question: What is the primary purpose of diagnostic techniques in primary health care?

options.A: To identify health problems and guide treatment
options.B: To increase the cost of patient hospital stays
options.C: To eliminate all potential risks of medication
options.D: To replace the need for physical examinations

explanation: Diagnostics are tools used to figure out what is wrong with a patient so the correct treatment can be started. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h1)

question: Why is checking for gender-based vulnerabilities important during a nursing assessment?

options.A: Social power imbalances directly influence treatment adherence and safety
options.B: Biological sex markers change entirely based on household income
options.C: Hospitals require this data solely for administrative billing records
options.D: Cultural expectations have no bearing on physical healing rates

explanation: You got it! Understanding domestic power dynamics and financial pressures helps us see why a patient might struggle to follow their treatment plan.

question: What is the main reason we monitor a child's growth at the clinic?

options.A: To detect growth problems before visible signs appear
options.B: To treat children who already have severe infections
options.C: To vaccinate children against common childhood illnesses
options.D: To provide free food supplies to low-income families

explanation: Spotting small changes in weight or height early lets you step in and help before severe malnutrition sets in. You've got this!

question: Why are open-ended questions so helpful during a patient chat?

options.A: They encourage patients to share more details
options.B: They prevent the patient from crying
options.C: They shorten the length of the clinical visit
options.D: They force the patient to answer with a simple yes

explanation: Questions starting with 'How' or 'What' invite patients to open up and tell their story in their own words.

question: Why do midwives and nurses group pregnancy signs into presumptive, probable, and positive categories?

options.A: To separate normal hormonal shifts from pathological illnesses
options.B: To calculate the precise delivery date without using ultrasound
options.C: To structure physical assessments and guide further testing logically
options.D: To determine the exact gender of the developing fetus early on

explanation: Categorizing signs helps you stay organized during antenatal care and know when it's time to run definitive tests. Great nursing logic!

question: What tool do primary care nurses commonly use to guide the treatment of minor ailments in basic clinics?

options.A: Direct telephone orders from federal ministers
options.B: Standing orders and treatment protocols
options.C: Surgical textbooks from teaching hospitals
options.D: International pharmaceutical marketing guides

explanation: Standing orders provide safe, approved guidelines for nurses to diagnose and treat common conditions at the primary level. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h3)

question: What type of germ is Salmonella?

options.A: A bacterium
options.B: A fungus
options.C: A parasite
options.D: A virus

question: What genotype represents a person who carries the sickle cell trait without having the full disease?

options.A: SS

options.C: SC
options.D: AS

question: What goes wrong in the body to cause the symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS)?

options.A: Accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques in the temporal lobes

options.C: Thrombus formation blocking blood flow in the middle cerebral artery
options.D: Autoimmune destruction of central nervous system myelin

explanation: In MS, the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and strips away the protective myelin coating on nerve fibers, slowing down signals.

question: What is a major difference between standard examination gloves and surgical gloves?

options.A: Surgical gloves are strictly sterile and have longer cuffs
options.B: Examination gloves are always thicker and tougher
options.C: Examination gloves come in precise numbered hand sizes
options.D: Surgical gloves are only used for drawing blood

explanation: Surgical gloves are sterile and feature longer cuffs to cover your gown sleeves, keeping the operating field completely germ-free.

question: A patient with high cholesterol uses butter for all their cooking. What heart-healthy swap can you suggest?

options.A: Coconut oil
options.B: Olive or canola oil
options.C: Palm oil
options.D: Solid shortening

explanation: Liquid plant oils like olive or canola are rich in unsaturated fats, making them fantastic, heart-friendly swaps for solid butter!

question: Which antibody class is mostly found in body secretions like breast milk and saliva?

options.A: IgD
options.B: IgG
options.C: IgA
options.D: IgE

explanation: Secretory IgA is our body's frontline defender in wet areas! It guards mucosal linings in our respiratory and digestive tracts, and is proudly passed to babies through breast milk.

question: When is the right time for a nurse to document a medication in the patient's chart?

options.A: Only if the patient experiences a negative side effect.
options.B: Before drawing up the medication in the treatment room.
options.C: Immediately after the medication is given.
options.D: At the end of the shift during the final handover report.

explanation: Exactly right! Documenting right away prevents accidental double-dosing by another nurse who might think the dose was missed.

question: A client with schizophrenia is stable and ready for discharge from a tertiary psychiatric hospital. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Keep the client admitted for another year to prevent any possibility of relapse
options.B: Advise the client to stop taking medications since their mood is now normal
options.C: Prepare a discharge summary and link the client to their local primary health clinic
options.D: Send the client home without informing local clinic staff

explanation: Great nursing care means bridging the gap! Writing a good summary and linking the patient to their local clinic ensures they won't default on their meds.

question: A 34-week pregnant mum comes in with painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Placenta previa
options.B: Placenta accreta
options.C: Chorioamnionitis
options.D: Placental abruption

explanation: Spot on! Classic textbook sign: painless, bright red bleeding late in pregnancy is a major red flag for placenta previa, where the placenta sits low over the cervix.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of long-term untreated hormone hypersecretion?

options.A: Cardiomegaly and increased risk of heart failure
options.B: Severe muscle weakness and brittle bone structure
options.C: Joint degeneration and chronic physical pain
options.D: Permanent shrinkage and complete disappearance of all bones

question: What safety check must you always perform before sending a patient for an MRI scan?

options.A: Excessive exposure to sun rays
options.B: Hidden metal objects and implants
options.C: Low levels of vitamin C
options.D: A history of drinking cold water

explanation: MRI machines use super strong magnets! Checking for metal keeps patients safe from flying objects or damaged implants like pacemakers.

question: Which group of people faces a much higher risk of experiencing interpersonal violence?

options.A: Retired corporate executives
options.B: Middle-aged professional athletes
options.C: Pregnant women and young children
options.D: Healthy young adult males living by themselves

explanation: You got it! Vulnerable groups like pregnant women, children, and older adults statistically experience higher rates of abuse and neglect.

question: How does aldosterone help raise blood pressure once it is released during the RAAS cascade?

options.A: It forces the heart to beat much faster
options.B: It causes the kidneys to retain sodium and water
options.C: It relaxes blood vessels throughout the body
options.D: It triggers the thirst center in the brain

explanation: Aldosterone signals the renal tubules to reabsorb sodium, pulling water along with it to increase blood volume and pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which fungal infection is a major cause of meningitis in patients with advanced HIV/AIDS seen in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Sporotrichosis ulcers
options.B: Cryptococcal meningitis
options.C: Aspergillus pneumonia
options.D: Dermatophyte ringworm

explanation: Correct! Cryptococcal meningitis is a serious opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients, and spotting it early saves lives on the wards.

question: Which board must review and approve any research involving human participants before data collection starts?

options.A: Institutional Review Board
options.B: Hospital Maintenance Committee
options.C: Financial Audit Committee
options.D: Nursing Licensing Board

explanation: The IRB acts as a safety shield, checking research plans to protect human participants from harm.

question: What happens to the heart muscle fibers during Ventricular Fibrillation?

options.A: They beat together in a slow, steady rhythm
options.B: They rest without any electrical signals at all
options.C: They become completely stiff and cannot relax
options.D: They twitch randomly without pumping any blood

explanation: During VF, the heart muscle fibers flutter and twitch chaotically like a bag of worms. Because they aren't working together, no blood is pumped to the body.

question: Which type of research focuses mostly on numbers, math, and statistics?

options.A: Quantitative
options.B: Ethnographic
options.C: Qualitative
options.D: Phenomenological

explanation: Fantastic! Think 'Q for Quantity'—quantitative research deals with numbers and statistical analysis.

question: What do we call the grief family members feel *before* their loved one actually passes away?

options.A: Post-mortem grief
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Acute distress syndrome
options.D: Complicated grief

explanation: It's called anticipatory grief because the family is already mourning the expected loss while the patient is still alive and fighting.

question: During the dry season, which water source is most risky for catching Guinea worm?

options.A: An open, stagnant surface pond used for bathing
options.B: A sealed overhead tank storing treated municipal water
options.C: A rapid-flowing mountain stream with rocky beds
options.D: A deep concrete borehole with a hand pump

explanation: Spot on! Open ponds easily get contaminated when people soak their painful, worm-filled blisters in them. You're thinking like a true community health nurse!

question: What is the primary public health goal of proper food storage?

options.A: To reduce the cost of grocery bills
options.B: To improve the taste of meals
options.C: To make cooking faster every day
options.D: To prevent foodborne illnesses

explanation: Keeping food properly stops harmful bacteria and germs from multiplying, which directly protects people from getting sick. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h1)

question: Why are run charts particularly useful for busy clinical nursing units?

options.A: They require very little statistical training to read
options.B: They replace the need for writing patient care notes
options.C: They automatically dispense patient medications safely
options.D: They permanently eliminate all hospital infections

explanation: Because they are simple and visual, clinical staff can easily interpret them without needing advanced statistical skills. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h1)

question: Unlike fats and carbohydrates, why do we need to eat protein-rich foods every single day?

options.A: Muscles consume all available protein within four hours
options.B: The liver destroys all stored amino acids overnight
options.C: The body does not have a dedicated storage depot for protein
options.D: Proteins evaporate quickly through the skin pores

explanation: Our bodies store extra carbs as glycogen and extra fat in adipose tissue, but we don't have a storage warehouse for protein. That's why daily dietary intake is a must!

question: A community refuses to bring sick relatives to the clinic because of rumors that nurses cause infections. How should you respond?

options.A: Ignore the community and wait until they come voluntarily
options.B: Threaten the villagers with police arrest for disobedience
options.C: Engage community leaders with clear, respectful health education
options.D: Close down the primary health center until they apologize

explanation: Wonderful nursing approach! Building trust through community leaders and patient education is key to clearing up dangerous rumors.

question: What is a key nursing action when caring for a patient taking a diuretic medication?

options.A: Check pupil reactions every fifteen minutes
options.B: Accurately monitor intake and output
options.C: Encourage a high-sodium snack diet
options.D: Restrict the patient from walking entirely

explanation: Spot on! Tracking what goes in and what comes out tells us if the diuretic is doing its job safely without causing dehydration.

question: Why are open-air markets often cheaper for food shopping in Nigeria than large supermarkets?

options.A: They do not require any form of monetary currency exchange
options.B: They only sell imported items that have expired
options.C: They avoid high markups for packaging and retail overhead costs
options.D: They receive government subsidies that lower all food prices

explanation: You nailed it! Open-air markets bring produce straight from farms without all the expensive branding, packaging, and high shop rents.

question: What can you find living inside a mature parasitic egg?

options.A: Free-floating viral particles
options.B: An adult reproducing worm
options.C: Active bacterial colonies
options.D: A fully formed or developing larva

explanation: Depending on how mature it is, the egg holds either early cells or a fully ready-to-hatch larva. You're crushing it!

question: Why might a patient in early shock still have a normal blood pressure reading?

options.A: Blood pressure monitors are usually inaccurate in emergencies
options.B: Kidneys immediately stop producing urine to save pressure
options.C: Fluid volume only affects the health of the heart
options.D: The body uses compensatory mechanisms like vasoconstriction

explanation: Our amazing bodies fight back! The nervous system tightens blood vessels and speeds up the heart to keep blood pressure normal at first, even if fluid is low.

question: A nurse notices more children losing weight in the months right before the new harvest. What activity helped spot this trend?

options.A: Individual genetic sequencing
options.B: Surgical theater auditing
options.C: Hospital pharmacy inventory check
options.D: Community nutritional status monitoring

explanation: Spot on! Tracking how nutrition changes across different seasons helps nurses spot recurring health issues in the whole community before they get out of hand.

question: A patient has heavy postpartum bleeding and a soft, boggy uterus. What should you do first?

options.A: Prepare the patient for an immediate MRI scan
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.C: Perform bimanual uterine massage
options.D: Insert a nasogastric tube for decompression

explanation: Massaging the uterus helps the muscle contract tightly, which closes off bleeding blood vessels. Great nursing intervention!

question: Why does quality improvement focus mainly on systems rather than individuals?

options.A: Because faulty systems are usually the root cause of errors
options.B: Because systems are easier to replace than human workers
options.C: Because individual nurses cannot change their daily habits
options.D: Because hospital managers do not care about staff actions

explanation: Spot on! Mistakes usually happen because a workflow or process is tricky, not because a nurse is careless. Fixing the system helps everyone succeed.

question: Which of these is allowed on a full fluid diet, but NOT on a clear fluid diet?

options.A: Plain water
options.B: Transparent beef broth
options.C: Clear apple juice
options.D: Plain milk

explanation: Clear fluids you can see straight through (like water or broth). Full fluids include cloudy items like milk and custard!

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely on just one method to check a patient's nutrition?

options.A: Patients usually refuse to answer dietary recall questionnaires alone
options.B: Hospital policies strictly require at least four different diagnostic tests
options.C: Lab values and physical signs can be influenced by acute illness or hydration
options.D: Single methods are too expensive for routine primary health clinics

explanation: Things like fluid changes can mess with lab numbers quickly, so combining a few tools gives you a much clearer, more reliable picture.

question: Which of the following is NOT a true barrier to assertive nursing practice?

options.A: Intimidation by experienced medical colleagues
options.B: Fear of being labeled as a difficult troublemaker
options.C: Having clear, updated hospital policies on safety
options.D: Cultural norms that discourage questioning seniors

explanation: Clear safety policies actually support and encourage nurses to speak up, rather than acting as a barrier. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h4)

question: What do we call all the chemical reactions that happen inside the body?

options.A: Responsiveness
options.B: Homeostasis
options.C: Differentiation
options.D: Metabolism

explanation: Great job! Metabolism is just the word we use for all the building up and breaking down of substances happening inside your cells to keep you going. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: In nursing safety terms, what is a 'near-miss'?

options.A: An error that is caught just in time before it reaches the patient
options.B: A minor allergic rash that goes away without medical treatment
options.C: A patient who refuses to take their prescribed medication
options.D: A drug that expired on the shelf and was thrown away safely

explanation: A near-miss is a lucky catch! It's an error spotted right before it harms the patient, giving the team a great chance to fix the system so it doesn't happen again.

question: You're a community nurse at a local market. Which activity is a great example of primary prevention for hypertension?

options.A: Admitting every market trader with high blood pressure to the intensive care unit
options.B: Distributing free blood pressure medication to people who already have severe stroke symptoms
options.C: Teaching market traders how to reduce salt in local meals and encouraging daily walks
options.D: Referencing advanced surgical guidelines for treating blocked coronary arteries

explanation: Brilliant! Teaching healthy eating and active living helps people protect their hearts before high blood pressure has a chance to develop.

question: What is the primary focus of medical services for special children?

options.A: Providing routine immunizations for infants
options.B: Meeting the unique developmental and physical needs of children with disabilities
options.C: Managing surgical emergencies in school-aged children
options.D: Treating only acute infectious diseases in hospitals

explanation: These specialized services focus on children who require extra medical, physical, or developmental support beyond standard care. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h1)

question: Due to physical immaturity, which medical complication is especially common in pregnant adolescents?

options.A: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.B: Primary pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Chronic autoimmune thyroiditis
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Spot on! Young mothers face a higher risk of developing pregnancy-induced hypertension and preeclampsia compared to older women.

question: Why are nurse managers usually involved in management audits?

options.A: To connect executive policies with actual bedside practices
options.B: To write new financial accounting laws for the ministry of health
options.C: To punish staff members who make clinical documentation errors
options.D: To replace the hospital chief executive officer during emergencies

explanation: Nurse managers are the amazing bridge between big hospital bosses and everyday patient care. Their input helps auditors see how administrative choices truly play out on the ward!

question: What is the main danger of constantly using an 'accommodating' (always giving in) style at work?

options.A: Building up personal resentment and professional burnout
options.B: Violating mandatory hospital accreditation standards
options.C: Creating aggressive conflict with every team member
options.D: Improving long-term interprofessional communication

explanation: If you always say yes and push your own needs aside, you'll eventually burn out and feel quietly bitter.

question: Which combination of vital sign changes makes up Cushing's triad (a sign of high pressure inside the brain)?

options.A: Hypertension, tachypnea, high fever
options.B: Widening pulse pressure, bradycardia, irregular respirations
options.C: Hypotension, tachycardia, shallow respirations
options.D: Narrow pulse pressure, tachycardia, rapid breathing

explanation: Cushing's triad is a critical warning sign! Watch for high blood pressure with a wide gap between top and bottom numbers, a very slow pulse, and weird breathing.

question: An 8-month-old baby is brought in with a cough and fast breathing. What sign tells you the baby needs antibiotics for pneumonia?

options.A: A slight decrease in daily milk intake
options.B: A clear nasal discharge and sneezing
options.C: Elevated respiratory rate for age while calm
options.D: A low-grade fever that responds to tepid sponging

explanation: Correct! Fast breathing while the baby is calm is a key clinical sign of lower respiratory infections like pneumonia.

question: What is 'data architecture' when talking about Electronic Health Records?

options.A: The structural framework that organizes how information is stored and retrieved
options.B: The electrical wiring inside hospital bedside monitor screens
options.C: The physical concrete building where computer servers are locked
options.D: The security guard schedule for the hospital IT department

explanation: Don't let the big word scare you—data architecture is just the digital blueprint or filing system that keeps electronic records organized so you can find them quickly. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h4)

question: How many hours of fasting are typically required before a standard GTT begins?

options.A: No fasting is needed
options.B: 18 to 24 hours
options.C: 8 to 14 hours
options.D: 2 to 4 hours

explanation: An overnight fast of 8 to 14 hours establishes an accurate baseline blood glucose level before the test beverage is consumed. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h3)

question: A low blood pressure warning pops up on your bedside monitor screen. Which computer cycle stage just happened?

options.A: Storage
options.B: Output
options.C: Input
options.D: Collection

explanation: Output is what the computer shows back to you on a screen or printer after it finishes processing the data.

question: What is the correct temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.A: Plus 15 degrees Celsius to plus 25 degrees Celsius
options.B: Minus 2 degrees Celsius to zero degrees Celsius
options.C: Plus 2 degrees Celsius to plus 8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Minus 15 degrees Celsius to minus 25 degrees Celsius

explanation: Keep this safe range in mind! +2°C to +8°C keeps most routine refrigerated vaccines cool and happy without freezing them.

question: What is the number one thing that encourages young people to open up and share sensitive health info with a nurse?

options.A: Free mobile phones
options.B: Presence of tribal leaders
options.C: Free meals at the clinic
options.D: Guaranteed confidentiality

explanation: Trust is everything! Teens need to know their secrets are safe with you before they'll feel comfortable talking about their health.

question: What is the main job of the rehab nurse within the healthcare team?

options.A: Prescribing physical therapy exercises and ordering diagnostic imaging tests
options.B: Reinforcing therapy skills and coordinating daily care around the clock
options.C: Providing formal legal counseling for insurance claims
options.D: Performing major orthopedic surgeries to correct bone deformities

explanation: Nurses are with the patient 24/7. We tie all the therapies together and keep the healing going round the clock. You are the heartbeat of the ward!

question: Why does a patient with acute gastroenteritis experience watery diarrhea?

options.A: Pathogens trigger excess fluid and electrolyte secretion into the gut
options.B: Kidneys dump excess water directly into the large intestine
options.C: The stomach completely stops all digestive enzyme production
options.D: The liver stops producing bile needed to bind stool together

explanation: Toxins and cellular damage force the intestinal lining to secrete large quantities of water and salts, overwhelming the bowel's ability to absorb them. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h2)

question: How does Quality Assurance differ from simple quality control?

options.A: QA focuses entirely on equipment, while control focuses on patients
options.B: QA is proactive and systemic, while control usually catches errors after they occur
options.C: QA is done once a year, while control is done daily
options.D: QA only applies to doctors, while control applies to nurses

explanation: Think of QA as setting up safety nets across the whole system ahead of time, whereas quality control is more like checking things after the job is done to catch any slip-ups.

question: A study shows a link between carrying a cigarette lighter and getting lung cancer. What role does smoking tobacco play here?

options.A: It is a confounding or underlying variable connecting the two
options.B: It is a zero-correlation factor with no medical relevance
options.C: It is an experimental intervention created by the researcher
options.D: It is a statistical error made during data entry

explanation: You got it! Lighters don't cause cancer directly—smoking tobacco is the underlying habit driving both things.

question: What is the basic structural unit of compact bone tissue?

options.A: Trabecula
options.B: Osteoid
options.C: Osteon
options.D: Periosteum

explanation: The osteon, or Haversian system, is the cylindrical functional unit that makes up the bulk of compact bone. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h2)

question: In which position should you place a patient who is having an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy?

options.A: High Fowler sitting upright
options.B: Supine flat on the back
options.C: Left lateral position
options.D: Prone face down on the bed

explanation: Lying on the left side is safest—it keeps the airway open and lets any saliva drain out easily without choking them.

question: Why is high blood pressure often called the 'silent killer'?

options.A: Blood pressure monitoring devices fail to detect early stage elevations
options.B: It only causes severe medical emergencies during deep nighttime sleep
options.C: Symptoms only appear after the patient stops taking prescribed pills
options.D: Patients rarely experience noticeable symptoms until serious organ damage occurs

explanation: Spot on! High blood pressure usually creeps up quietly without any warning signs, which is why routine checks are so important in clinical ward practice.

question: Oops! During insertion, your catheter accidentally slips into the female vagina. What should you do next?

options.A: Wash the same catheter with antiseptic soap and try again
options.B: Leave it temporarily as a landmark and insert a new sterile catheter
options.C: Push it deeper into the vagina to find the correct opening
options.D: Remove it and immediately push that same tube into the urethral meatus

explanation: Smart nursing move! Leaving that stray tube in the vagina stops you from accidentally making the same mistake twice on your next try.

question: Which side effect do many patients report during the first few weeks of taking an Efavirenz-based regimen?

options.A: Vivid dreams or dizziness
options.B: Permanent blindness
options.C: Complete loss of hearing
options.D: Sudden hair color changes

explanation: Correct! Efavirenz can temporarily cause quirky side effects like vivid dreams or feeling dizzy, but these usually fade away after the first few weeks.

question: What is the main benefit of agencies working together in community health?

options.A: It reduces the number of rural health clinics
options.B: It pools resources and expertise to tackle complex health needs
options.C: It puts all healthcare services inside major airports
options.D: It removes the need for nursing licenses

explanation: Exactly! When different agencies team up, they share funding, knowledge, and hands-on help to solve big health problems together.

question: Why do we need good 'organising' skills after making a nursing care plan?

options.A: It completely stops all workplace conflicts among nurses
options.B: It eliminates the need for any staff supervision during the shift
options.C: It prevents confusion and resource wastage by defining clear roles
options.D: It guarantees that hospital funding will increase next year

explanation: Great thinking! When you organise well, everyone knows their specific duties for the shift, which stops people from stepping on each other's toes or wasting scarce supplies.

question: How does male andropause usually differ from female menopause?

options.A: It involves a slow and gradual decline in hormone levels
options.B: It causes an immediate and complete stop to all sperm production
options.C: It affects every single man at exactly age fifty years
options.D: It occurs during early adolescence rather than late adulthood

explanation: Correct! Unlike the quicker hormone drop in female menopause, men experience a very gradual, slow decrease in hormone levels as they age.

question: Which of these is a tertiary drug information source?

options.A: An original clinical trial published in a journal
options.B: A standard pharmacology textbook
options.C: A PubMed database search engine index
options.D: An unpublished case report from a ward

explanation: Well done! Textbooks and drug guides are tertiary sources because they summarize lots of existing medical knowledge into one quick-to-read place.

question: What is a major role of state-level primary health care bodies in Nigeria?

options.A: Building private international airports
options.B: Collecting local market taxes for traditional rulers
options.C: Appointing village chiefs in rural communities
options.D: Supervising LGA activities and procuring bulk medical supplies

explanation: State bodies provide mid-level oversight, supporting local governments with supplies, training, and technical guidance. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T7#GNS124_U1_T7_h5)

question: What do we call it when a nurse physically walks through a factory floor to observe how safe the workers' habits are?

options.A: Financial auditing
options.B: Job safety analysis
options.C: Biological sampling
options.D: Workplace walkthrough

explanation: A workplace walkthrough lets healthcare pros see real working conditions and habits firsthand so we can help keep workers safe.

question: Why are nurses considered frontline defenders in occupational health?

options.A: They spot workplace dangers and help protect staff and patients
options.B: They write all the labor laws for the country
options.C: They inspect building foundations for structural damage
options.D: They buy and sell safety gear for factories

explanation: Nurses work closely with people in clinical and industrial spaces, putting them in a prime position to notice health risks and advocate for safety. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good characteristic of effective instructional materials?

options.A: Relevance to the topic
options.B: Scientific accuracy
options.C: Clarity and simplicity
options.D: Outdated clinical practices

explanation: Instructional materials must always contain current, accurate information; outdated practices can compromise patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h4)

question: How do sedatives stop brain cells from firing electrical signals?

options.A: By destroying the chemical messengers before they reach neighboring cells
options.B: By opening chloride channels to make the inside of the neuron more negative
options.C: By blocking sodium channels so electrical charges leave the brain completely
options.D: By increasing the speed of calcium flow across the cellular membrane

explanation: When negative chloride ions rush inside the cell, it becomes much harder for the nerve cell to fire off an electrical signal. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T2#GNS223_U6_T2_h3)

question: When a woman is diagnosed with cervical cancer, which two cell types are most commonly involved?

options.A: Sarcoma and transitional cell carcinoma
options.B: Melanoma and small cell carcinoma
options.C: Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma
options.D: Lymphoma and clear cell carcinoma

explanation: You've got this! Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma make up the vast majority of cervical cancers. They develop from the two main types of cells found on the cervix.

question: You want to ask ten exact admission questions across five different hospitals without changing a single word. Which format fits best?

options.A: Open-ended dialogue
options.B: Structured interview
options.C: Unstructured interview
options.D: Semi-structured interview

explanation: You nailed it! A structured interview is rigid on purpose—it keeps every single question identical so your data stays consistent across different sites.
